summary: Approval webhook rejects SSO assertions missing phone claim causing 403 on Access Request approvals
description:
Issue summary:
Support Portal approval attempts return 403 when the user's SSO assertion does not include a phoneNumber claim. The approval microservice validates an 'auth_level' decision which currently depends on the presence of a phoneNumber (SMS MFA) claim produced by Okta for some users. Impact:
- On-call and support engineers cannot approve access requests for a subset of employees (mostly those with MFA via Okta Push only).
- Affected flows: Support Portal -> approval-webhook -> approval-microservice -> RBAC grant.
Environment: production, us-east region.
Observed: Approver clicks Approve -> UI shows "Approval failed (403)" -> Support Portal logs show 403 from approval-microservice: "insufficient_auth - missing phone claim". Not all users are affected; those with Okta SMS enrollment produce the phoneNumber claim and succeed.
Expected: Approval should succeed for users who meet MFA policy (Okta Push or SMS), or at minimum the microservice should evaluate 'amr' (authentication methods) rather than relying on phoneNumber claim which is inconsistently emitted.
Steps to reproduce:
1) Using a non-privileged account that has Okta Push MFA only (test accounts created by identity team), create an access request in Support Portal for a teammate.
2) Sign in as approver (standard prod approver) and attempt to approve the request.
3) Observe UI 403 and inspect approval-microservice logs (see logs below).
Logs / snippets:
- approval-ms logs at 2026-03-10T15:42:19Z: "decision=DENY reason=missing_phone_claim user=employee-uuid-12 amr=["push"]"
- support-portal ui error: HTTP 403 from approval-api: {
  "error": "insufficient_auth",
  "detail": "phoneNumber claim not present in SAML assertion"
}
- Okta assertion sample for affected user (redacted): amr: ["push"] (no phoneNumber attribute)
Notes: Identity team rolled an Okta attribute-mapping change two weeks ago; mapping for 'phoneNumber' is only emitted when SMS is enrolled. We believe approval-ms policy predates the Push MFA rollout and expects phoneNumber as proxy for second factor, which no longer holds in all org cases.

investigation_notes: 2026-03-10: Initial reproduction with test accounts. Confirmed difference between 'sms' and 'push' amr values and presence/absence of phoneNumber attr.
2026-03-10: approval-ms rule logic examined. Decision code block in service checks for 'phoneNumber' attribute as boolean gate (legacy).
2026-03-11: Identity change log: IDENTITY-MAP-2026-02-26 removed phoneNumber emission for push-only users to reduce token PII. Change attached in Confluence page.
2026-03-11: Performed manual SAML assertion inspection via saml-tracer from test browser sessions; confirmed phoneNumber removed for push-only users.
2026-03-12: Ran unit test covering amr=["push"] and no phoneNumber -> currently DENY. Implemented local unit test and updated logic to evaluate amr list (allow if amr contains 'push' or 'sms').
2026-03-12: Executed canary with feature flag 'approval_fallback_amr' in staging. 200 approvals in staging with push-only and sms accounts all succeeded after change.
resolution: Workaround applied: Identity team declined temporary phoneNumber re-add. Implemented service-side fallback: approval-microservice now checks 'amr' authentication methods and treats 'push' as acceptable second factor when feature flag enabled. Patch PR github.com/redwood-inference/approval-ms/pull/482 under review. Planned rollout: enable feature-flag in prod for 10% traffic 2026-03-14 then 100% 2026-03-15 after 6h validation. Post-incident action: update runbook and remove hard dependency on specific PII attributes; add integration test that simulates both push and sms assertions.
